:::{#thm-pd-submatrix}
#### Leading blocks of a positive definite matrix are positive definite

Let $\matr{X}$ be a $p \times p$ positive definite matrix (@def-positive-definite),
and for $1 \le k \le p$ let $\matr{X}_k$ be its top-left $k \times k$ block,
with entries $x_{ij}$ for $i, j \le k$.
Then $\matr{X}_k$ is positive definite.
In particular, every diagonal entry of a positive definite matrix is positive.

:::

::: proof

$\matr{X}_k$ is symmetric, because $\matr{X}$ is.
For $\vecf{u} \in \reals^k$ with $\vecf{u} \ne \vzero$,
let $\vx = (u_1, \ldots, u_k, 0, \ldots, 0) \in \reals^p$, which is nonzero. Then

$$
\ba
\tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{X}_k \vecf{u}
&= \sum_{i=1}^{k} \sum_{j=1}^{k} u_i\,x_{ij}\,u_j
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult, @def-dot-product)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{p} \sum_{j=1}^{p} x_i\,x_{ij}\,x_j
&& \text{(the added terms have a factor } x_i = 0 \text{ or } x_j = 0 \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx} \matr{X} \vx
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult, @def-dot-product)}
\\
&> 0.
&& \text{(} \matr{X} \text{ positive definite)}
\ea
$$

(Here $x_i$ denotes entry $i$ of $\vx$, and $x_{ij}$ an entry of $\matr{X}$.)
For the diagonal entry $x_{ii}$, use $\vx = \vecf{e}_i$ (@def-indicator-vector):
$\tp{\vecf{e}_i} \matr{X} \vecf{e}_i = x_{ii} > 0$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-pd-submatrix}
#### A quick necessary test

$\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ is positive definite (@exm-pd-operations),
and its diagonal entries $2, 2$ and its $1 \times 1$ leading block $[2]$ are positive.
The test can only rule matrices out:
$-\matr{I}_2$ has negative diagonal entries, so it is not positive definite,
even though $\det(-\matr{I}_2) = (-1)(-1) - 0 = 1 > 0$ (@def-determinant);
a positive determinant alone does not make a matrix positive definite.
And positive diagonal entries are not enough:
$\matr{D} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ of @exm-positive-definite has them
but is not positive definite.

:::
